title: Linearize a gravity-drained tank
equipment: Gravity-drained water tank with variable-speed inlet pump
physicalPurpose: Derive and validate local transfer functions for a nonlinear gravity-drained tank.
principalTechnique: Operating-point linearization and first-order transfer functions
objective: Derive a first-order transfer function for a gravity-drained tank at three operating points and use executable error evidence to decide where each local model is valid.

simplifications: Constant tank area, liquid properties, and outlet coefficient
No pump, sensor, overflow, transport-delay, or disturbance dynamics
Local models use a 100 ms forward-Euler teaching realization of the analytically derived tangent equations

baseline.limitation: A tangent model derived at low level cannot represent the nonlinear tank over its complete operating range.

change.decision: Use a local model only with its operating point, declared range, and validated error evidence.

abortPredicates: Any flow or level is nonfinite
A level leaves its hard limit
The sample interval or physical parameters differ from the prediction
safety.restorationMode: Return flow deviation to zero and restore all three declared equilibria
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Physical tank tests require reviewed pump, outlet, overflow, low-level, containment, and emergency procedures plus immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Derive and validate a local transfer function without mistaking it for a global plant model.

learning.context: A pumped tank drains through a fixed gravity outlet whose flow changes with the square root of level.
learning.reason: The constant-outlet integrator from Lesson 33 cannot predict level-dependent equilibrium and response speed.
theory: Linearization replaces a nonlinear relation by its tangent around a declared equilibrium.
Deviation variables and a zero-initial-deviation Laplace representation produce a local first-order transfer function.
Gain, time constant, and pole vary with operating level; the model has no finite zero or dead time.
learning.workedPrediction: At 0.25, 0.50, and 0.81 m, calculate the three equilibrium flows, gains, time constants, poles, and small-step level changes before running.
practicalPreparation: Verify operating points, units, parameters, 100 ms sampling, quality, limits, open-loop authority, and Simulation evidence class.
Declare the 0.30 cm small-step error limit and label the large step outside validity before viewing results.
learning.baseline: Apply the low-level tangent assumption globally and explain why the square-root outlet invalidates it.
learning.change: Run three derived local models beside three nonlinear tanks, then execute a separately restored large-step boundary case.
learning.comparison: Compare synchronized nonlinear and local-model levels only after checking units, operating points, and settling eligibility.
learning.validation: Require all small-step final errors below 0.30 cm and retain the greater-than-5 cm large-step divergence as validity-boundary evidence.
learning.explanation: The tangent slope changes with level, producing increasing local gain and time constant at higher operating points.
learning.transfer: Lesson 35 generalizes pole-zero interpretation across real plant classes before controller design.
